title: the public first step is not runnable
expected: a newcomer can follow the actual published, signed CLI installation route.
recheck: follow the final public instructions on a clean supported Mac, then create/run an app.
observed: The Install section promises a future standalone command and shows git clone <repository>.
impact: A newcomer cannot complete the public first step.

title: the tutorial omits the execution instructions
expected:
a reader knows the starting prerequisites, where to put the source, and how to see
  and test the result before proceeding through the editing steps.
recheck: an uncoached reader reaches the first screen and runs the final journey using the text.
observed: The tutorial begins with a Tao block without filename, setup or execution instructions.
impact: An uncoached reader must guess how to reach the first screen and run its test.

title: the front door mixes future and initial release surfaces
expected:
the phase-1 entry point clearly distinguishes supported web authoring from later
  releases and repository-development capabilities.
recheck: Read the Install section, platform statement and complete command table against the phase-1 public artifact. Confirm every later or repository-only surface has explicit availability.
observed: The platform and command tables combine web, native, Android, Studio and shipping without phase labels.
impact: Readers can choose a route unsupported by the initial public artifact.

title: navigation choices read as one label
expected: a reader can distinguish the two destinations and the active choice.
recheck:
inspect and operate both tabs at phone and desktop widths. This is an observation of
  the web-rendered tutorial; it makes no claim about native tabs.
observed: The captured navigation reads LibraryAbout without a visible gap or selected treatment.
impact: Readers cannot readily distinguish destinations or the active choice.

title: phone sections are separated by a large empty area
expected: Short and long phone lists remain visually connected with intentional spacing while preserving useful adaptive desktop behavior.
recheck: judge short and long lists on a phone; preserve useful adaptive behavior on desktop.
observed: A large empty area separates the single Reading row from the Finished heading.
impact: Related lists feel disconnected on the small display; this is a design judgment.

title: dark scenario retains the light presentation
expected:
explicitly support an intentional light-only showcase or provide an accepted
  dark presentation. The tutorial does not currently promise a dark theme, so this is not a
  demonstrated violation of its written behavior.
recheck: Repeat the exact captured scenario and inspect the result.
observed: Requested dark scenario retains the light presentation; both inspected phone images have identical digests.
impact: Dark appearance remains a design decision; the written tutorial does not promise dark mode.

title: desktop evidence contains a transient zoom indicator
expected: A settled app capture contains app content with no transient review zoom indicator.
recheck: capture a settled app view with review overlays absent.
observed: The desktop screenshot includes a transient 100% zoom indicator.

title: one starter scenario has no usable image
expected: The exact tablet-dark scenario reaches a usable captured state and receives an explicit image review.
recheck:
reproduce that exact scenario and inspect its image. Do not classify the underlying
  cause as an app defect from the timeout alone.
observed: Notebook devices/tabletDark did not reach a usable capture state.
impact: The dark tablet visual state is unreviewed; no product cause is established.

title: The wrapping state remains unreviewed
expected: A usable wrapping-state image supports an actual readability judgment.
recheck: Reproduce rows/wrapping, capture it, and inspect long-title readability.
observed: HNReader rows/wrapping timed out during per-cell capture.
impact: Long-title wrapping remains visually unreviewed despite other successful captures.
